The Commander-in-Chief's propensity to attend sporting events almost resulted in his presence at another NFL game. But it ultimately didn't.

On Tuesday, Kristen Holmes of CNN reported that President Trump was expected to attend the Week 6 game between the Steelers and Buccaneers in Tampa. Later in the day, she reported that Trump would not be making the trip.

It would have been the third NFL game attended by Trump during his current term. He was present for Super Bowl LIX in New Orleans between the Chiefs and Eagles. Last year, he attended a Lions-Commanders game in Maryland, making him the first sitting president to attend a regular-season game in nearly 50 years.

Two years ago, in the weeks preceding the election that resulted in his second term, Trump attended a Sunday night game between the Jets and Steelers.

It remains to be seen whether he shows up for an NFL game before the midterm elections, which happen in 20 days. The Commanders are currently scheduled to host the Eagles on Sunday, November 1 — two days before the in-person polls officially open.

item.title: Packers Film Room: Attacking after an interception
item.description: Breaking down the Packers offensive play after an interception against the BEars
item.content:encoded:
If you watch football for any amount of time, you have no doubt heard the same talking points repeated hundreds of times. Thousands of times. An ocean of times, spreading out over the vast and speckled horizon. Some of those things are good, some of them are bad, and some simply roll off your back and find a nice home somewhere outside of your mind.

One of those things is this: “after forcing a turnover, the offense should take a deep shot.” While it’s not something you can do every time, it is something that you can have success with, and it’s something you’ll see coaches looking to do. Whether it’s a straight deep shot or a trick play, you’re trying to catch the defense on the first play of the series when they’re not expecting to be out there. Maybe they were in the middle of sitting down with a coach to look at the last possession. Maybe they were in the middle of drinking a Gatorade and are now cursing their QB for making their rest so short.

The thinking is that maybe you can catch a defense that is not quite as focused as they could be. It’s something the Packers took to heart in their Week 5 win over the Chicago Bears and had some nice success with.

While the Packers had 5 turnovers on the day, I’m only going to look at the plays following the 3 interceptions, as the score was 31-7 midway through the 4th quarter when the first of two fumbles occurred.

Play 1: 1st & 10, 5:32 remaining in the 1st quarter

The Packers are up 7-0 when Tyson Bagent throws a pass to Luther Burden that is tipped up by Javon Bullard and intercepted by Xavier McKinney:

That sets the Packers up at the Bears 45 yard line. This is the least aggressive of the calls, but they’re still looking to push it with the primary concept. The Packers are in 12 personnel (1 RB, 2 TE, 2 WR). They shift to a balanced formation (an in-line TE to each side, a WR split wide to each side, the RB aligned directly behind the QB).

They’re running deep curls off play action against a two-high look. It’s a good call against that defense, but the Bears linebackers are dropping back deep, taking those away.

With the linebackers dropping that deep, Jordan Love [10] takes the checkdown to MarShawn Lloyd [32] under the linebackers.

Not much, but 6 yards is 6 yards.

Play 2: 1st & 10, 00:34 remaining in the 3rd quarter

The Packers are up 23-7 when Tyson Bagent throws to Colston Loveland and is, once again, intercepted by Xavier McKinney. McKinney is initially dropping down to pick up the motion TE, but, when that man stays back to block, he drops back to the middle, reads Bagent’s eyes and jumps the throw.

That sets the Packers up at their own 45 yard line. Once again, they come out in 12 personnel in a balanced formation, but this time they’re looking to drive the ball downfield. Love sees something pre-snap and he Cans the call to a variant of High Cross. It looks like Matthew Golden [0] and Christian Watson [9] are going to be running deep over routes, crossing each other in the middle of the field. Instead, they both reverse course and break back to their respective sidelines.

Watson gets a little tied up in his route, but Golden does a nice job at creating separation off the line, keeping that separation down the field and breaking back outside over the defender. Golden really shows his speed here: he gives up quite a bit of ground to the inside on the release, but he’s able to burn up that distance throughout the route and create late separation as he breaks back outside.

With the single high safety breaking to the middle of the field, Golden has a lot of room to work back outside to.

Love lays it up to the outside. Instead of tracking the ball to his outside shoulder (and potentially giving the safety a chance to knock it free), Golden jumps up and twists back to high-point the ball.

36 yard gain.

Play 3: 1st & 10, 12:49 remaining in the 4th quarter

The Packers are up 31-7 when Case Keenum throws to Rome Odunze in the red zone and is intercepted by Ty’Ron Hopper. Hopper returns it 19 yards, setting the Packers up on their own 19.

Once again, the Packers are looking to push it. They trot out Yankee, a two-man concept that has a receiver from one side (Watson) running a deep over route and the receiver from the other side of the formation (Golden) running a deep post route. The Packers are in 12 personnel and shift to a balanced formation. The Bears are in a single-high look and Love is reading the single-high safety.

That safety drops down to pick up Watson on the crosser, giving Golden inside leverage on his man. So Love chucks deep to Golden. The defender from the other side is looking to fall under this route as soon as Watson is passed off to the safety in the middle (good communication there), but the throw is far and Golden is fast.

Once again, Golden goes up for the ball and comes down with a 50 yard catch (in front of a tumbling ref).

Here’s what Jordan Love did on the play immediately following an interception by the defense: 3/3 for 92 yards (30.7 YPA). Not too shabby.

Albums listened to: Margot & The Nuclear So and So’s – The Dust of Retreat; Josefin Öhrn + The Liberation – Cherry

item.title: Week 6 AP NFL Power Rankings: Patriots and Packers are on the rise
item.description: The Arrowhead Pride team ranks the league from top to bottom.
item.content:encoded:
Football is a beautiful, hilarious, and unpredictable game. The ball is oddly shaped, one of the worst teams can beat a good team any given day, and it’s ultimately the best drama we watch on television on a weekly basis.

Week 5 had it all.

It started with the winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers upsetting the Dallas Cowboys in Dallas. The drama continued Sunday morning, as the Philadelphia Eagles bumbled their lead with only eight seconds remaining after a special-teams gaffe against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London.

Both “Sunday Night Football and “Monday Night Football” games went into overtime.

All four NFC East teams played and finished the week 0-2-2. New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo tried to win it for the Washington Commanders in overtime, but quarterback Jayden Daniels said, “No thanks.”

We saw the first major trade before the deadline: the Arizona Cardinals shipped wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. to the one-win Houston Texans.

Three teams remain undefeated, while an equal number remain winless.

The season is just starting to heat up, and the Arrowhead Pride staff is back with updated power rankings.

Biggest riser: Green Bay Packers +10

Biggest faller: Dallas Cowboys -7

This week, along with myself, staff voters were: Maurice Elston, Caleb James, Ron Kopp Jr., Rocky Magana, Jared Sapp, and Matt Stagner.

1. San Francisco 49ers (1st)

Kyle Shanahan has done an impressive job as head coach to start the season. What appears to be the cream of the NFL crop this season remains on top.

2. Kansas City Chiefs (2nd)

I fully expect a classic Chiefs-Chargers thriller, in which we make the Chargers look 5-0 instead of 0-5, yet squeak out a win in spectacular fashion to preserve Andy Reid’s amazing post-bye-week record.

3. Baltimore Ravens (6th)

We were subjected to the annual Snoop Huntley primetime game. And it did not disappoint.

4. Buffalo Bills (5th)

Congratulations to Josh Allen on winning the first overtime game of his career. Running back James Cook tried to give the game away twice before it happened, however.

5. Jacksonville Jaguars (3rd)

The London Jaguars won in incredible fashion on Sunday.

6. Minnesota Vikings (7th)

Undoubtedly, Week 5 saw Kyler Murray’s best performance as a Viking. If he plays that well, this team could be a legitimate NFC contender.

7. Seattle Seahawks (4th)

Sam Darnold hasn’t looked the same since his glute injury, and aside from JSN, this offense lacks the juice it once had. Chiefs fans owe the 12 a thank you.

8. Los Angeles Rams (8th)

This season is on pace to age head coach Sean McVay a good 30 years.

9. Cincinnati Bengals (10th)

The bye week could be coming at a great time for the Bengals to reset and get some dinged-up players healthy. They then face a favorable upcoming slate of opponents. Their next seven: Ravens, Titans, Falcons, Steelers, Commanders, Saints, and the Browns.

10. Chicago Bears (9th)

Head coach Ben Johnson wanted blowouts. I’d say 31-7 suffices.

11. New England Patriots (16th)

The Pats were a Bills’ blocked field goal away from being tied for first place in the AFC East. Who would have guessed that three weeks ago?

12. Denver Broncos (13th)

I’m worried that despite the Broncos winning games, Bo Nix isn’t playing well enough to justify paying him 60 million per season.

13. Detroit Lions (15th)

The Lions actually could have won this week without scoring over 30 points.

14. New York Giants (17th)

Cam Skattebo owes Jayden Daniels a big thank you.

15. Philadelphia Eagles (11th)

That had to be a long flight home. Horrible way to lose a football game. Three straight losses after a 2-0 start.

16. Green Bay Packers (26th)

The Bears-Packers rivalry is one of the best in sports. I think that’s the only reason the Packers turned it around as they did on Sunday.

17. Carolina Panthers (20th)

The Panthers remain in first place in the NFC South without having played a game.

18. Las Vegas Raiders (12th)

The combined record of teams the Raiders beat: 1-14

The combined record of teams the Raiders lost to: 7-2

19. Pittsburgh Steelers (22nd)

Jaylen Warren is small but mighty.

20. Atlanta Falcons (23rd)

Apparently this team can only function if Michael Penix is under center. And unfortunately for the Falcons, his biggest problem is availability.

21. Dallas Cowboys (14th)

You’ve reached an all-time low when the hot dog guy in the concourse is trash-talking on your quarterback.

22. Cleveland Browns (18th)

Should have seen this one coming. They may have won three in a row, but I’m sorry. You just can’t be taken seriously from week to week, losing to the Jets.

23. Indianapolis Colts (19th)

The very definition of “mid.”

24. Houston Texans (25th)

I’m not sure the trade for Marvin Harrison Jr. solves any of this team’s issues.

25. New Orleans Saints (21st)

The Saints’ offense has plummeted back down to earth. Facing the Vikings’ defense certainly doesn’t help matters.

26. Arizona Cardinals (24th)

That Week 1 upset over the Chargers looks increasingly less impressive the further it gets in the rearview mirror. And it’s never a good sign to trade away a top-5 draft pick three years later. 

27. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (30th)

You could see Todd Bowles breathe a heavy sigh of relief on the sideline, as he likely saved his job with the upset win over the Cowboys. Also, give it up for KU alum Jalon Daniels.

28. New York Jets (28th)

It’s almost Halloween, and the Jets aren’t completely irrelevant.

29. Washington Commanders (27th)

I never saw the label “game manager” as a negative trait for a quarterback. And this game is a perfect example as to why. Your franchise quarterback simply cannot make that mistake at the end of the football game. But man, was it entertaining.

30. Miami Dolphins (31st)

It’s now week 6. The Dolphins still haven’t held a lead this season.

31. Los Angeles Chargers (29th)

“I’m not sure what the message is,” Jim Harbaugh said after the Chargers’ latest loss which dropped them to 0-5. Yeah, this team’s season is toast.

32. Tennessee Titans (32nd)

One of my good buddies is a Titans fan. He told me this team may legitimately be one of the worst teams in NFL history.

item.title: NFL Power Rankings entering Week 6: Someone has to win NFC East among disappointing Cowboys, Commanders, Giants and Eagles
item.description: The entire NFC East had a miserable Week 5. But someone has to win that division, even if none those teams are good.
item.content:encoded:
NFC East:Cowboys | Giants | Eagles | Commanders
NFC North: Bears | Lions | Packers | Vikings
NFC South:Falcons | Panthers | Saints | Buccaneers
NFC West:Cardinals | Rams | 49ers | Seahawks

AFC East:Bills | Dolphins | Patriots | Jets
AFC North:Ravens | Bengals | Browns | Steelers
AFC South:Texans | Colts | Jaguars | Titans
AFC West:Broncos | Chiefs | Raiders | Chargers

The NFC East has become the new NFC South, at least through five games. It is the worst division in football, at least from one measure. And the eye test.

The NFC East, which has just one team over .500, is the only division in which every team ranks 20th or worse in DVOA. The Dallas Cowboys are 20th, and that's the best standing among the teams. The Philadelphia Eagles are 23rd, the New York Giants are 27th despite being 3-1-1 and the Washington Commanders are 28th. That's a lot of bad football.

The oft-told joke from Sunday was that all four NFC East teams played in Week 5, including two against each other, and the division still went winless. That's because the Giants and Commanders tied, which everyone knows because of a management mistake at the end of the game by Washington that was hard to believe. But that's the NFC East.

The rules state the division has to send a team to the playoffs. It's tough to figure out which one it could be.

The Giants have the lead but over the last three weeks they have barely beaten the Titans and Cardinals, and tied the Commanders. Those three teams are a combined 2-12-1. Jameis Winston is fun and he played well Sunday but it seems hard to believe he doesn't blow up or that the Giants stay on top. But who's going to catch them? The Eagles' best game of the season was a loss on Sunday to the Jaguars, one that rivaled the Commanders for worst late-game management by a coaching staff.

Philadelphia's only two wins are near misses against the Commanders and Titans, who are a combined 1-8-1. The Commanders might have been a reasonable answer with a win on Sunday, but they blew the chance for that and the way the game ended could linger. Even if that isn't the reason Washington fades, the Commanders' shoddy defense might be.

That leaves the Cowboys. They are the highest ranked team in DVOA. The defense is really bad, ranking 32nd. But their offense is probably the best unit in the division, except the times it goes strangely quiet, like it did last Thursday night against the Buccaneers. Still, even with that strangely lethargic loss to the Buccaneers at home, it's easier to see Dallas turning things around than any of the other three teams.

None of the four teams look like they will end up deserving a postseason spot. There's a chance the winner of the division finishes under .500 like last season's NFC South, though there will be plenty of opportunities against bad opponents when they play intradivision games.

Someone will win the NFC East. Maybe it's the Cowboys. Or, based on the way they've all played this season, it might not really matter that much.

Here are the NFL power rankings after Week 5 of the NFL season:

32. Miami Dolphins (0-5, Last week: 32)

The good news for the Dolphins is they won't lose in Week 6. They have a bye. Good for the Dolphins to lose by only seven points against the Bengals on Sunday, but the true story of the game was a 28-10 deficit after three quarters. The Dolphins have trailed by at least 14 points in four of five games.

There are two main goals after the bye: getting one win to avoid the 0-17 questions, and finding out if Malik Willis can be the quarterback of the future. A decision in the 2027 NFL Draft looms. Willis was 1-for-7 passing for 22 yards with a minute to go in the first half Sunday. He threw two interceptions and lost a fumble. It wasn't good enough, and garbage-time stats don't fix that. Of 32 qualified quarterbacks he's 30th in adjusted EPA (expected points added) per play and 29th in success rate. It is hard to judge Willis fairly because there's not much talent around him, but he has to prove he can elevate his teammates.

"I will say this: We will need more consistency in our pass game in general for all 11 players to be better in order for us to take the next step," Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said.

31. Tennessee Titans (0-5, LW: 31)

Five games into Cam Ward's second season, the questions about benching him are starting.

"Cam is our starting quarterback," Titans head coach Robert Saleh said, according to the Associated Press. "We're going to give him every opportunity to be successful this year. We're going to continue working with him, grinding with him, and trying to help him get better."

Ward had just 170 yards on 36 pass attempts against the Texans. The Titans scored only three points. Tennessee is 3-19 in Ward's starts. He has 896 yards and three touchdowns in five starts this season. The Titans have to see it through with last year's No. 1 overall draft pick, but it doesn't look good so far this season.

30. Los Angeles Chargers (0-5, LW: 29)

The Chargers' starting offensive line on Sunday was impossibly desperate for Week 5 of an NFL season, or really any week of any season:

Left tackle: rookie fourth-round pick Travis Burke

Left guard: rookie sixth-round pick Logan Taylor

Center: rookie second-round pick Jake Slaughter

Right guard: Cole Strange, ranked 73rd of 75 guards in PFF grades

Right tackle: rookie sixth-round pick Alex Harkey

If the Chargers' situation seems beyond repair, it is. They were a bad team even when healthy, and they had numerous injuries to key players on Sunday. Justin Herbert has not played well at all, but against the Broncos it was hard to put all the blame on him considering the catastrophe of the line protecting him. It's hard to believe the Chargers' season is over — no 0-5 team has ever made the playoffs — but it's probably going to get worse before it gets better.

29. Arizona Cardinals (1-4, LW: 27)

Trading Marvin Harrison Jr. was best for everyone involved, but let's not celebrate the Cardinals too much for getting a second-round pick back in a trade with the Texans. Arizona got very little out of the fourth overall pick in a loaded 2024 NFL Draft. That's horrendous, even if the Cardinals recouped some value. As Bob McManaman of the Arizona Republic pointed out, the Cardinals have already moved on from four of the last six players they drafted in the top 10 overall: Josh Rosen, Kyler Murray, Isaiah Simmons and Harrison.

On Sunday, the Cardinals got shredded by the Lions' offense, and Arizona's offense did surprisingly little against a bad Detroit defense before some garbage-time yards and points. It's looking bleak in Arizona, as it usually does with this franchise.

28. New Orleans Saints (1-4, LW: 23)

It's time to give up on the Saints until they show they're a good team. They're now 30th in DVOA, ahead of only the Titans and Dolphins. New Orleans would be 0-5 if not for a second-half rally at Baltimore, which included a go-ahead touchdown on a controversial call. It looks now like the Saints got hot against a very soft second-half schedule last season and that momentum has not carried over.

The Saints, and particularly QB Tyler Shough, were dreadful against the blitz-happy Vikings. Shough had 96 yards, two interceptions and a 38.1 passer rating. Minnesota is a tough matchup but that's bad. The Saints had 142 yards as a team. They have some winnable games coming up (at Giants, vs. Steelers, vs. Browns, vs. Panthers) but they haven't shown they're better than any of those teams.

27. New York Jets (2-3, LW: 28)

The Jets figured out they should just get the ball to Garrett Wilson and watch good things happen. Wilson had 104 yards and a touchdown in a 17-12 win over the Browns. Wilson, who had seven catches, was targeted 11 times and no other Jet had more than four.

New York also leaned on its defense, a unit that had eight sacks and held Cleveland to a season-low 198 yards.

Wilson disappeared last season with injuries and a bad quarterback situation holding him back. He had 395 yards in seven games last year. This season he already has 374 yards and the Jets seem committed to running the offense through him.

"He's Garrett Wilson, and we think he can do that every single week," Jets quarterback Geno Smith told the media after the game. "He loves competing, he's a proven player. He makes plays when the ball comes his way. We've got to continue to find ways to get him the football, and once the ball is in his hands he'll make plays."

26. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (1-4, LW: 30)

One win changed the Buccaneers' outlook this season. Tampa Bay looked good in beating Dallas, with rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels playing well. Even though Baker Mayfield wants to return from a dislocated thumb in Week 6, via James Palmer of Amazon Prime Video, Daniels' play makes Tampa Bay less desperate to bring back its quarterback too soon.

The NFC South doesn't have a team over .500 so it's not like the Buccaneers are out of anything, even at 1-4. Tampa Bay hosts Pittsburgh in Week 6 and then faces Carolina and then Atlanta in a two-game stretch that could revive its season.

25. Washington Commanders (1-3-1, LW: 25)

Let's wait a moment to pile on Dan Quinn, Jayden Daniels and whoever else was responsible for the fiasco at the end of Sunday's tie. There were other issues. The Commanders allowed a field goal and three touchdowns on the Giants' first four possessions of the second half. They had a 27-13 lead with just over 11 minutes left and couldn't win. The Commanders couldn't make a play against Jameis Winston to clinch a victory. And with a chance to ice the game with a 27-20 lead or win the game in the final 1:43 of regulation or after a missed Giants field goal in overtime, the Commanders punted three times. Those were failures too and can't be forgotten.

And obviously the end of the game was inexcusable. The Commanders were rudderless as the clock ran out, and that's alarming. Quinn doesn't call offensive or defensive plays so a stupefying failure in clock management at the end is a really bad look for him. Daniels has to be more aware as well. It's not impossible for the Commanders to rebound from blowing a shot at a win Sunday, but it was embarrassing and will affect them all season in the NFC East race, if they ever get back in it.

24. Houston Texans (1-4, LW: 26)

Beating the Titans this season doesn't mean a whole lot. But at least the Texans looked good doing it. Their defense gave up a 58-yard drive and a field goal on Tennessee's first possession of the game. The rest of the day, the Texans allowed no points, 129 yards and no drive longer than 27 yards. C.J. Stroud played well, and while the running game still lagged at 2.9 yards per carry, it was good enough on offense.

The next question is whether Marvin Harrison Jr. can help the offense. The Texans must think so considering they sent a second- and seventh-round pick to Arizona for Harrison and a sixth-round pick. They need some punch in the offense. It's questionable if Harrison can come in and be an impact player in the middle of the season after having just five catches for 85 yards and a touchdown for Arizona in 2026. It's tough for any receiver to learn an offense and establish chemistry with a quarterback during a season. However, if it works it could transform Houston's offense. That's the Texans' gamble.

23. Indianapolis Colts (2-3, LW: 22)

Playing right after an international game is not easy. The Colts took a step back in Sunday's loss at Pittsburgh and it's fair to blame playing in London in Week 4. They missed tackles, especially on two long touchdowns by Jaylen Warren that turned the game around, and they repeatedly settled for field goals in the red zone. Indianapolis had improved in some areas over Weeks 3 and 4, but nothing looked good in a 34-22 loss to the Steelers.

"Go back to the fundamentals of technique," Colts head coach Shane Steichen said via the team's site, regarding tackling. "It was good last week, and then this week it wasn't as good as it needs to be, and so we got to keep working hard on that."

Next up for the Colts is a home game against the Titans, and that needs to be a win because after that they face road games against the 5-0 Vikings and 4-1 Jaguars.

22. Cleveland Browns (3-2, LW: 20)

The Browns were close to a much better day. Receiver Isaiah Bond was pressed into action after KC Concepcion's concussion and he had a big drop in a big moments and once ran out of bounds when it seemed he could have pushed upfield for more yardage. One drop came in the end zone and another was on a second-and-19 that could have given the Browns a first down just ahead of the two-minute warning. Those plays were huge in a five-point loss.

Still, the Browns failed to top 200 yards against a Jets defense that had just given up 492 yards to a Tyson Bagent-led Bears offense. Cleveland's 3-1 start came with some close wins and the Browns were due some regression. Week 6's game against the Ravens, who may be without Lamar Jackson, will be telling.

21. Atlanta Falcons (2-3, LW: 16)

With a minute to go in regulation, the Falcons led by eight points at home against a backup quarterback. The Ravens came back to win in overtime and the Falcons will look at that as a game that they should have won.

Now the Falcons have to worry about Michael Penix Jr. It was disheartening for the team and Penix that the quarterback was unavailable for overtime because of a rib injury suffered on a hard hit late in regulation. Penix has a long injury history dating back to college. He missed the first two games of this season while recovering from his third torn ACL. Even if Penix is available for the Falcons' next game, the injury issue isn't going away, and the Falcons have already shown they're one of the NFL's worst teams without him.

20. Dallas Cowboys (2-3, LW: 12)

The Cowboys are blowing a good opportunity in a bad NFC East. They gave away a game against the Ravens by mismanaging the final seconds of regulation. They lost at home last week as a big favorite to a Buccaneers team with an undrafted rookie quarterback.

The problem isn't hard to diagnose, and it's the defense. The Cowboys are 32nd in defensive DVOA, the exact spot they held last season. New coordinator Christian Parker hasn't been any better than old coordinator Matt Eberflus and the personnel additions haven't changed anything either. Team owner Jerry Jones gave the odd reason when he traded Micah Parsons that improving the run defense was a major part of the decision; the Cowboys have allowed an NFL-worst 842 rushing yards. Jones is already being asked if he'll remove Parker, and while the answer has been no, the Cowboys did add longtime defensive coach Mike Pettine to the staff this week.

19. Philadelphia Eagles (2-3, LW: 15)

Give the Eagles this: They battled hard in London and after 59:52 it looked like they would beat the Jaguars, who are one of the best teams in football this season. It was easily the Eagles' best performance this season. Absolutely nobody in Philadelphia wants to hear that after the last eight seconds, in which the Eagles kicked off, allowed a 53-yard return and a 57-yard field goal to inexplicably lose. The decision to let the Jaguars have a shot at a return was a clear mistake.

"I didn't make the right decision and I lost us that game," Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni said, via the team's site. "And that's what I said to our guys. And what hurts there is that the guys fought so hard and then I don't make the decision that I should make at the end of the game and I cost us that game and I put that fully on me."

Sirianni won a Super Bowl two seasons ago. Since then, the Eagles had a disappointing and drama-filled 2025 season and this season they're 2-3, with the two wins coming late against teams who are a combined 1-8-1. Add in the end of Sunday's game and Sirianni might be in trouble soon. Doug Pederson was fired three seasons after his Super Bowl win, for reference.

18. Green Bay Packers (3-2, LW: 24)

Through all the (justifiable) angst over the Packers' start, they're 3-2 coming off a blowout win over the Bears, who were the favorite to win the division. The Packers looked mostly poor during the first four weeks but they find themselves in a good place now.

There are things to clean up, but the trio of Jordan Love, Matthew Golden and Christian Watson might keep Green Bay in the playoff race. Love has played well despite little help from his offensive line, and on Sunday he had a great game with 367 yards. He completed five passes of 30 or more air yards, only the second time that has happened since ESPN Insights began tracking the stat. Golden has 397 yards and two touchdowns and Watson has been even better, with 474 yards and six touchdowns in five games.

"We kept our foot on the gas," Love said after the eye-opening 31-7 win over Chicago, according to AP. "Matt [LaFleur] was dialing it up. That's what it needs to look like, right there."

17. Pittsburgh Steelers (3-2, LW: 21)

Aaron Rodgers' stat line isn't perfect. His 59.8 completion percentage is the worst of his career as a starter. So is his 88.9 passer rating. But what he's doing at his age has been approached only by Tom Brady.

Not counting Brady, whose production in his 40s is an extreme outlier, no quarterback in his age-43 season (Rodgers turns 43 in December) has ever had more than 952 passing yards or six touchdowns in a season. Their teams combined for two wins in their starts, and both were from Vinny Testaverde in 2007. Testaverde had a bad 65.8 passer rating that season. Rodgers already has 1,234 yards, 10 touchdowns and the Steelers have won three of his starts, more than every other quarterback at his age combined, other than Brady.

Whatever happens the rest of this season, Rodgers' season is already historic for his age.

16. New York Giants (3-1-1, LW: 17)

The Giants should feel good to get a half of a win after Washington completely blew the end of the game, but New York blew a chance to win itself. In overtime they missed a 46-yard field goal and Cam Skattebo fumbled at Washington's 24-yard line. A tie felt like a win at the end, but that got the Giants off the hook for their own mistakes.

One absolute positive from the game was Malik Nabers. He followed up a 112-yard game by getting season highs with 11 catches and 121 yards. He scored the game-tying touchdown in the final two minutes of regulation. Even more encouraging, he played a season-best 89.9% of New York's snaps. He had not surpassed 80% in the first four games. It's safe to say Nabers is back to normal after last season's ACL tear.

15. Carolina Panthers (2-2, LW: 18)

David Tepper shouldn't get too many flowers for becoming a somewhat rational team owner, but he could have considered a coaching change after Dave Canales was 6-15 to start his time with the Panthers. Tepper had been going through coaches like paper plates before then. But ownership stayed the course and Canales has turned it around. He gave up play-calling duties to offensive coordinator Brad Idzik, and that setup has been a success. Bryce Young is having a career year, and even getting mentioned in early MVP conversations. Carolina's offense entered Week 5 ranking fourth in the NFL in both points and yards despite major offensive line injuries.

That looks great on Idzik, who could be a hot name in the head-coaching carousel next offseason if this continues. It also reflects well on Canales for recognizing what needed to change for the Panthers to improve after backing into an NFC South championship last season.

14. Denver Broncos (3-2, LW: 14)

For a 3-2 team, the Broncos should probably be lower in the rankings. The winless Chargers had numerous injury issues Sunday and yet the Broncos still trailed 17-10 with less than 10 minutes left. The Chargers' decision to go for it on fourth-and-1 at their own 41, and then not converting a quarterback sneak, turned around the game. The Broncos deserve credit for stopping that streak and rallying to win, but anyone thrilled with where the Broncos are after five games is ignoring the problem signs.

One of those problems could be Bo Nix. The Broncos are considered to have one of the NFL's best offensive lines. They have enough at receiver including Jaylen Waddle, whom Denver traded a first-round draft pick to acquire. Head coach Sean Payton took over play-calling duties, and that didn't immediately change the offense. When is Nix's role in the woes going to be examined? His passer rating has gone from 93.3 to 87.8 to 80.8 in his first three seasons. On Sunday, with Payton back calling plays, Nix had 123 yards passing against a decent Chargers defense that was without star safety Derwin James Jr. The Broncos can't change play-callers again. Nix needs to perform better. It doesn't get easier with a matchup against the Seahawks on Thursday night.

13. Detroit Lions (3-2, LW: 19)

The Lions' defense is likely to still be a problem, even though it played well against the Cardinals. Detroit's offense is just fine. Jared Goff has 12 touchdowns and no interceptions through five games, which puts him in rare company.

QBs to have 12 Passing TDs and 0 INTs through the first 5 games

2026 Jared Goff
2019 Russell Wilson

That's it. That's the list. pic.twitter.com/NQeqX5sat4

— BetMGM 🦁 (@BetMGM) October 12, 2026

But the engine of the offense is Jahmyr Gibbs. He leads the NFL with 747 yards from scrimmage and nine total touchdowns. That's a pace of 30.6 touchdowns, in range to challenge LaDainian Tomlinson's single-season record of 31. Gibbs didn't deny he has eyes on that record.

"Oh, yeah, for sure. Yeah, I'm trying," Gibbs said, via MLive.

12. Las Vegas Raiders (3-2, LW: 10)

An early East Coast start against a Patriots team that felt energized after a win over the Bills was a tough spot for the Raiders. Still, it was a troubling performance on both sides of the ball. The Raiders' offense didn't get much going, and averaging 2.1 yards per carry was a big reason. Perhaps Ashton Jeanty, who was a game-time decision with foot and ankle injuries, should have sat for a week. He had 27 yards on 10 carries. Vegas' defense was shredded by Drake Maye, who had 374 yards and four touchdowns passing and another one rushing. The Raiders' defense hadn't been bad through four weeks, so it can be excused to a tough day against a good quarterback who is starting to heat up.

It's one bad game after four promising ones, so it's not time to panic. But the next two games will tell the story: The Raiders host the Bills and Rams the next two weeks.

11. New England Patriots (3-2, LW: 13)

Drake Maye isn't a bad quarterback. Go figure. After naysayers got their licks in during Maye's three-game slump to start the season, which was an extension of his postseason issues, Maye has 643 passing yards, seven passing touchdowns, 79 rushing yards and a rushing score in his last two games. Those games came against the Bills and Raiders, who had one combined loss before facing New England. Stunning, but a 24-year-old quarterback who was one vote from winning MVP last season might still be good.

"It's just fun to see Drake smiling big on the sidelines," Patriots linebacker Robert Spillane said, via SB Nation. "That confidence is obviously back, and just watching him lead and push the ball down the field was fun."

10. Los Angeles Rams (2-3, LW: 8)

The Rams can play the what-if game. What if Week 1 hadn't been in Australia? What if the officials had gotten a flubbed defensive pass interference call right at Denver in Week 3? And what if Harrison Mevis' field goal hadn't gotten blocked in overtime on Monday against the Bills? But they are also a veteran team and know the NFL is a results business. A team that got heaps of Super Bowl hype all offseason is 2-3.

The special teams is a recurring problem. The blocked field goal Monday night could be looked at as a bad break for many teams, but the Rams' special teams have been a problem for a while. Huge special teams mistakes led to losses in their final two games against the Seahawks last season, including in the NFC championship game. It shouldn't be a surprise that the special teams let them down with the game on the line Monday. 

9. Cincinnati Bengals (3-2, LW: 11)

Joe Burrow wasn't too thrilled after Sunday's win over the Dolphins. His assessment of the team after five games? "Gotta be better. Gotta be better," Burrow said, according to transcripts. When asked in what ways the Bengals need to be better, he said, "Everywhere."

"I think just not good enough all around, team-wide," Burrow said. "I think if we want to be the team that we think we're going to be, you got to be better than that."

The Bengals didn't play that bad. It speaks to how poor the Dolphins are that leading 28-10 into the fourth quarter isn't good enough. But Burrow is trying to get his team to a higher level, which is reasonable going into their bye. The first game back from the bye is huge. The Bengals go to Baltimore to face the Ravens.

8. Chicago Bears (3-2, LW: 6)

It's hard to rank the Bears. On one hand, they were horrendous in a 31-7 loss to the Packers. Also, they have scored 60 points in four games since scoring 59 in the opener. They've had two games scoring seven or fewer points. A defense that had been playing well gave up too many big plays against the Packers, who had 358 yards passing.

Of course, everything will change soon when Caleb Williams comes back. It's unfair to judge a team too harshly when it went 2-1 with two different backup quarterbacks. And Williams is close to returning from a hamstring injury.

"He's on track," Bears head coach Ben Johnson said, via Bears Wire. "We'll see if that's Atlanta [for Week 6] or after. I think it's going to be close."

Once Williams returns, it'll be easier to get a clear read on the Bears.

7. Minnesota Vikings (5-0, LW: 9)

Justin Jefferson's return changed the Vikings' offense. Not many receivers are capable of making the circus catch he did for a touchdown with three Saints defenders in his vicinity.

The offense playing its best game, in the first game this season that Kyler Murray and Jefferson were healthy throughout, was a big story. The other one is the Vikings' unrelenting blitz strategy. Coordinator Brian Flores sent a blitz on 23 of 27 Saints dropbacks (85.2%), according to Pro Football Focus. New Orleans had 87 net passing yards and 142 total yards. Blitzing as much as this season's Vikings have is a fascinating experiment, and there's no sign the Vikings are going to ease off it.

6. Seattle Seahawks (3-2, LW: 2)

Moving the Seahawks down this far after a home loss to our No. 1 team is probably too punitive. The Seahawks will likely move up soon. But they are just 3-2.

One move that hasn't gotten enough criticism is letting Kenneth Walker III leave in free agency. Walker is an NFL MVP candidate for the Chiefs. He has transformed their offense and been one of the best players in the league. Meanwhile the Seahawks' running game is floundering. A fumble by George Holani deep in Seahawks territory that was recovered for a 49ers touchdown epitomized a running game going nowhere. Seattle is 30th in EPA per rush play. First-round draft pick Jadarian Price going on IR hasn't helped but he was struggling before his injury.

"That's a position where you can find guys," Seahawks general manager John Schneider said in March to 710 Seattle Sports, regarding Walker's departure.

It's hard to criticize the Seahawks, who were a tremendous champion last season and will be good again. But letting Walker go looks like a big mistake.

5. Jacksonville Jaguars (4-1, LW: 4)

The Jaguars did not play well in London. Head coach Liam Coen's passing on short field goals twice, and the Jaguars' failure to convert on fourth down either time looked like it was going to be the story coming out of a 17-16 loss. Then in the final eight seconds the Jaguars got a long kickoff return and kicked a field goal for a 19-17 win over the Eagles.

"Guys stayed the course and we ended up squeaking away with a win," Coen said, according to the team's site. "It ain't pretty, but it's gritty. That's what it comes down to. It's what this team has been. It's what the team is. I love that group."

That's life in the NFL. Questionable decisions fade away when a team wins, even when it's a miracle. The Jaguars stay in London and face the 1-4 Texans next Sunday in a game that could give Jacksonville a massive lead in the division just six weeks into the season.

4. Baltimore Ravens (4-1, LW: 7)

Sunday night's Ravens win can carry them for a long time. The Ravens won on the road without Lamar Jackson, despite trailing by eight points with a minute to go in regulation. Tyler Huntley came through when it was needed but the Ravens needed a lot more than just Huntley. They rushed for 208 yards. The defense wasn't perfect but did a fair job holding down a hot Falcons offense — seven of Atlanta's 23 points came off a defensive touchdown.

Sunday night's comeback win felt like it made up for the one loss when they let down in the fourth quarter against the Saints, and Jackson's ankle injury isn't considered a long-term issue. A win like Sunday could be a turning point in Baltimore's season.

"That's a big step for our team," Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said, according to the team's transcripts. "And if we let it be, it can be a launch point for us to really, really get this thing rolling."

3. Buffalo Bills (4-1, LW: 5)

Josh Allen is one of the few players for which it doesn't really matter what's going on around him. He's always going to give the Bills a chance to win. Allen did need one assist on Monday night at the Rams and got it when linebacker Greg Rousseau blocked a field goal in overtime. That, and Allen's dramatic play that included several key runs (he had 121 yards rushing), was enough to overcome a defense that couldn't get a key stop, another quiet night from Dalton Kincaid and an injury that kept DJ Moore out, two fumbles by James Cook, including a big one in overtime, and everything else. Allen has one MVP and Monday night should position himself as the favorite to win another. The Bills are a flawed team, particularly on defense, but Allen is playing at such a high level they're still 4-1 and clearly a Super Bowl contender.

2. Kansas City Chiefs (4-0, LW: 3)

Jets pass rusher David Bailey is the leading early contender to win NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year after his three sacks on Sunday, bringing him to five on the season. But Chiefs cornerback Mansoor Delane has a case too.

Delane is off to a great start to his pro career. Entering Monday, he ranked fourth among all cornerbacks in Pro Football Focus' grades. According to PFF he has allowed just nine catches for 80 yards in three games (he missed one because of injury). Quarterbacks have a 46.5 passer rating when throwing his way. Delane was a polarizing pick after the Chiefs traded a third- and fifth-round pick to move up three spots and take Delane sixth overall. It seemed like an overpay. But the Chiefs have to be thrilled with what they've seen so far.

1. San Francisco 49ers (5-0, LW: 1)

A win at Seattle leaves no doubt who is the No. 1 team after five weeks. The 49ers have played very well. Their offense being hyper efficient should have been expected. Their defense, even with Nick Bosa playing just two games and having no sacks, has been the big surprise.

The 49ers are fourth in defensive DVOA, fourth in EPA allowed per play, ninth in success rate allowed, third in points allowed and sixth in yardage allowed. The key has been the linebacker play of Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw, though Greenlaw was ejected and suspended one game for head-butting helmet-less Seahawks linebacker Ernest Jones IV on Sunday. The 49ers lost defensive coordinator Robert Saleh in the offseason and that could have been a big blow after Saleh did a tremendous job last season. But new coordinator Raheem Morris is also doing an excellent job.

item.title: Week 6 NFL Power Rankings: Are the 49ers the unquestioned best team in the NFL?
item.description: The Niners have done nothing but show they’re the NFL’s best team so far.
item.content:encoded:
The San Francisco 49ers continued stacking up wins on Sunday, this time beating the Seattle Seahawks 32-29 in a thriller that went down to the final possession.

Playing banged up offensively, the 49ers capitalized on Seattle’s mistakes in a seven-turnover game, as they improved to 5-0 and remained unbeaten atop the NFC West.

While the 49ers remained unbeaten, the Rams and Seahawks both lost, widening San Francisco’s lead in the NFC West heading into Week 6. With the changes in the NFL this past week, let’s take a look at the industry’s power rankings for Week 6.

ESPN: No. 1

“Under new coordinator Raheem Morris, the Niners rank fifth in yards per play allowed (4.7) and have limited big plays as well as any team in the league,” ESPN’s Nick Wagoner wrote. “But they have struggled to get off the field consistently. The Niners rank 20th in third-down defense, giving up a first down on 40.8% of their opportunities. As a result, their defense has been on the field for 31 minutes, 12 seconds per game, which ranks 23rd in the NFL.”

Rest of top five: Chiefs, Bills, Seahawks, and Jaguars.

The 49ers’ biggest area for improvement is their third-down defense, which ranks 20th in the NFL. Still, despite all their injuries, the 49ers have found ways to keep winning.

NFL.com: No. 1

San Francisco remained No. 1 on NFL.com’s power rankings of the week, and NFL.com’s Nick Shook also pointed out the defense, but in a more positive light.

“There’s something special cooking within San Francisco’s defense, a unit that has every excuse to be average, at best, but continues to exceed expectations,” Shook wrote. “While the final score (32-29) doesn’t suggest it, Sunday’s win in Seattle was a defense-driven victory — and a big one for the team’s confidence as a true Super Bowl contender.”

Rest of top five: Chiefs, Seahawks, Ravens, and Jaguars.

There seems to be a consensus on the Chiefs, who are also undefeated and coming off their bye week. Meanwhile, most remain extremely high on the Seahawks, which only further validates the 49ers’ win on Sunday.

The Athletic: No. 1

Just like the two above, the 49ers are the top team in The Athletic’s weekly power rankings, with their resume standing out through five games.

“No team has a better resume than the 49ers, who overcame a rare so-so game from Brock Purdy in Seattle,” The Athletic’s Chad Graff and Josh Kendall said. “This time, it was San Francisco’s defense that led the way, limiting the Seahawks to just 4.2 yards per play. Oh, and Mike Evans and George Kittle certainly do not look like they are 33 years old.”

It’s a good sign that the 49ers are winning in different ways, especially considering the gauntlet of a schedule they face to end the season.

Rounding out the top five were the Chiefs, Bills, Vikings, and Jaguars. Despite being one of three undefeated teams, the Vikings haven’t received much love in the power rankings ahead of Week 6, but they did here.

Sports Illustrated: No. 1

The 49ers jumped from No. 5 last week to No. 1 in Connor Orr’s latest power rankings.

“The 49ers lead the league in wins…and players who are on injured reserve,” Orr wrote. “I heard a theory on Monday while making calls that stuck with me: the teams that are at the biggest advantage in the NFL are the ones with continuity at head coach, playcaller and quarterback over a multi-year period, especially during a season in which 10 head coaching jobs shifted this offseason. The steadiness of the Shanahan-Purdy partnership is shining.”

Rounding out the top five were the Jaguars, Chiefs, Bills, and Seahawks.

CBS Sports: No. 1

The 49ers remained atop Pete Prisco’s weekly power rankings for CBS Sports, and he believes this could be their year to win a Super Bowl.

“San Francisco 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan hasn’t won a Super Bowl. That doesn’t mean he isn’t a great coach,” Prisco wrote. “If last season, in which he won 12 games with an injury-ravaged team, didn’t prove how good he is at leading the 49ers, this year is doing just that. The 49ers are 5-0 after going to Seattle and beating the Seahawks on Sunday, doing it with a defense leading the charge, rather than the Shanahan-led offense.

“The 49ers limited the Seattle running attack, forced four turnovers, one of which was recovered in the end zone for a touchdown, and had five sacks, the most they’ve had in a game since 2024. They did it without star pass rusher Nick Bosa. First-year defensive coordinator Raheem Morris is using a much more aggressive scheme than past Shanahan coordinators, and it’s showing up in takeaways and sacks. The coverage is tighter. Combine that with Shanahan’s offensive wizardry and an MVP-type start for quarterback Brock Purdy, and it’s easy to understand why the 49ers sit atop my Power Rankings. Going to Seattle and beating the defending champs sends a loud message to the rest of the league. This team is really good.

“As for Shanahan, his greatness as a coach might not truly be earned until he wins a Super Bowl. That’s just the way it is. He came close when his Jimmy Garoppolo-led 49ers had a lead against the Kansas City Chiefs in Super Bowl LIV after the 2019 season, only to see Patrick Mahomes rally to win it. They came close again four years later in Super Bowl LVIII, with Purdy and Co. pushing Mahomes and the Chiefs to overtime before losing. This team, provided it stays healthy, has a real shot at getting back there for Shanahan. For now, they are the league’s best team with a schedule that might not be as tough as expected before the season. Plus, they already have victories over division rivals in the Rams and Seahawks. This could be Shanahan’s year to win one.“

Rounding out the top five here are the Chiefs, Vikings, Jaguars, and Bills.

item.title: Examining the roster ties between Patriots, Jets ahead of Week 6
item.description: The ex-Patriots and ex-Jets in the fold for Sunday at Gillette Stadium.
item.content:encoded:
Some familiar faces will meet again at Gillette Stadium.

Between the active rosters, practice squads and reserve lists, seven players in the fold for Sunday’s AFC East matchup have been both New England Patriots and New York Jets during their NFL careers.

Here’s a glance through the list of former Patriots and former Jets ahead of the 1 p.m. ET kickoff.

NEW YORK

Andrew Beck, fullback — Entering the NFL as part of the 2019 undrafted class in Foxborough, Beck was waived by the Patriots at the 53-man roster deadline following his rookie training camp. The Texas Longhorns product was claimed by the Denver Broncos that Labor Day weekend and has since taken the field for 92 games, including 24 starts. A past recipient of the NFL’s Salute to Service Award, his career includes 31 receptions for 259 yards and five touchdowns. The 30-year-old fullback has also lent a hand with one rushing touchdown. Beck made his way back to the AFC East as a futures signing in 2025 after stints with the Green Bay Packers and Houston Texans.

Chukwuma Okorafor, offensive tackle — Eleven months into a one-year deal, the Patriots released Okorafor before waiting for the 2025 league year to open. The offensive tackle played 12 snaps on the blindside in his lone New England start before being replaced and placed on the left squad list. He reverted to the reserves for the remainder of that 4-13 campaign after the club’s roster exemption expired. Okorafor has gone on to sign consecutive one-year pacts with the Jets. He has appeared in 19 games during his time in Florham Park, with 62 of his 63 downs coming in the kicking game. The 29-year-old originally entered the league with the Pittsburgh Steelers in the third round of the 2018 draft at No. 92 overall. A Western Michigan alum, his run spans 97 games and 60 starts.

NEW ENGLAND

Morgan Moses, offensive tackle — Voted a team captain out of training camp, Moses has played 1,349 offensive snaps for the Patriots since arriving on a three-year contract as an unrestricted free agent in 2025. The 35-year-old right tackle has started all 22 games in the regular season over that span. Entering the NFL out of Virginia in the third round of the 2014 draft at No. 66 overall, Moses finds himself with 188 appearances and 180 starts on his odometer. He made previous stops with the Washington Commanders and Baltimore Ravens. And he’s been a Jet twice, as well, beginning in 2021 and circling back in 2024 via trade. A total of 30 starts were notched during his previous tours in the division.

Alijah Vera-Tucker, guard — The Patriots landed Vera-Tucker on a three-year agreement as NFL free agency kicked off in March. The veteran addition has started all five contests at left guard this fall and stayed in for 100 perfect of the workload for the offensive line. He finds himself the team’s last ironman at this point in October. Selected by the Jets in the first round of the 2021 draft class at No. 14 overall, Vera-Tucker appeared in 43 out of a possible 85 games with his previous employer. The past PFWA All-Rookie honoree from USC sustained a torn triceps in 2022, a torn Achilles in 2023 and a torn triceps in 2025. When healthy, the 27-year-old has started every game he’s appeared in during his time in the league.

Greg Van Roten, guard — Van Roten was placed on New England’s injured reserve at the end of September after suffering a thigh injury during his first start of the year at right guard. He had been called upon there after tenured incumbent Mike Onwenu landed on injured reserve due to a fractured ankle. The 36-year-old Van Roten visited Gillette Stadium during training camp and soon returned to a sign a one-year deal. A veteran of 147 games, including 106 starts, the former All-Ivy League offensive tackle out of Penn began his career as an undrafted rookie in 2012. He has been a member of nine different NFL organizations in addition to the CFL’s Toronto Argonauts over the years since then. Count the Jets among the previous. Van Roten started 23 of his 30 games before being released in the spring of 2022 with one year left on a three-year pact.

Xavier Newman-Johnson, guard — After being hosted by the Patriots as a free agent midway through September, Newman-Johnson signed to the practice squad. The 27-year-old interior offensive lineman had been released from the Jets’ practice squad before headed to Foxborough. He stands 25 games into his run in the NFL and with a handful of starts. Originally entering the league with the Tennessee Titans as an undrafted free agent in 2022, the Baylor product spent parts of two campaigns with head coach Mike Vrabel’s former team before heading to the AFC East. Newman-Johnson, who resided between the practice squad, 53-man roster and injured reserve while in Florham Park, has seen 338 snaps on offense and 68 snaps on special teams.

Leonard Taylor III, defensive tackle — The Patriots added Taylor to the practice squad one October ago after he cleared waivers via the Jets. The 27-year-old defensive tackle went on to become a seven-time standard elevation on the journey to Super Bowl LX and reached a futures contract in February. Nine tackles and a blocked field goal in the AFC title game had been registered by then. Taylor worked his way onto the initial 53-man roster entering 2026. He got the first sack of his stay with the defending division winners last Sunday. The 2024 undrafted free agent by way of the Miami Hurricanes checked into 16 games while with New York, tallying 27 tackles, 2.5 sacks and a pair of batted passes.

item.title: Broncos vs Seahawks preview: Denver looks for TNF win
item.description: The Broncos are coming off a divisional road win & Seattle is coming off a divisional loss. Here is the TNF preview.
item.content:encoded:
If not for an unfortunate injury, this likely would have been the Super Bowl matchup last February.

Alas, it’s what we have for Thursday Night Football to start Week 6. For Bo Nix and the Denver Broncos (3-2), they’re coming off a win over the Los Angeles Chargers. For Sam Darnold and the Seattle Seahawks (3-2), they’re coming off a tough home loss to the San Francisco 49ers.

It’s a clash of old AFC West divisional rivals who will also be rocking their throwbacks. For what it’s worth, the Broncos are unbeaten in their snot rocket-fueled sky blue and orange D beauties.

Denver is a +2.5-point home underdog at FanDuel Sportsbook to the Seahawks. The total sits at over/under 40.5 points, with a lean toward the over at -115.

Offensive Rankings 

Seattle: Seventeenth in total offense (328.0 yards per game), 17th in rushing offense (106.0 YPG), 16th in passing offense (222.0 YPG), eighth in scoring offense (26.8 points per game).

Denver: Thirtieth in total offense (269.0 yards per game), 25th in rushing offense (86.2 YPG), 25th in passing offense (182.8 YPG), 26th in scoring offense (19.4 points per game).

Defensive Rankings   

Seattle: First in total defense (251.2 yards per game), 11 in rushing defense (100.4 YPG), first in passing defense (150.8 YPG), eighth in scoring defense (21.0 points per game).

Denver: Twenty-second in total defense (347.4 yards per game), 29th in rushing defense (145.2 YPG), ninth in passing defense (202.2 YPG), 13th in scoring defense (22.2 points per game).

Here are the MHR staff’s keys to Thursday night’s game.

Win the line of scrimmage on defense

For a defense that is likely to be down the best cornerback in the NFL against arguably the best receiver in the NFL, the Broncos pass rush has to consistently harass, hit, and pressure Darnold. To be effective on Thursday night, the Broncos front is going to have to get home and do the job. If you want to take the big-play ability from Seattle, don’t give Darnold time and make him see ghosts. “Get home” also means Denver stopping the run. This is one helluva challenge for the Broncos, but winning the line of scrimmage on defense sets them up for victory. — Ian St. Clair

Win the TOP battle

The Broncos offense hasn’t done a great job controlling the clock. Against a team like Seattle, this will be a major key to the game. Keep the Seahawks defense on the field and limit the opportunities they will have on offense to generate a big play. — Tim Lynch

Create turnovers

For the Broncos to win this week, the defense will need to continue creating turnovers. The Seahawks, with JSN against a very banged-up secondary, are likely to generate a lot of offense. If the Broncos can take it away, they have a great shot at beating the champs. — Sadaraine

Block

For the love of all that is holy, be better on the offensive line. Watching the Chargers just get in the backfield for almost an entire game was really disheartening. The blame for all the offensive woes can be placed on Sean Payton, or Bo Nix, or a disappearing Courtland Sutton, or a juiceless J.K. Dobbins, but who is going to perform behind an o-line that has so much in common with a spaghetti strainer? It’s been bad. It could be disastrous against the defending Super Bowl champs. — Adam Malnati

Score more points than Seattle

Using deep analytics, I have come up with the foolproof way for the Broncos to improve to 4-2. They have a 3-0 record when outscoring their opponents and a 0-2 record when they do not. They are also undefeated when wearing their throwbacks. So, score more points than the Seahawks while wearing the throwbacks, and the Broncos will come away with the victory. — Scotty Payne

Broncos have to be better on third down

If teams can’t convert on third down, they usually lose the game. Last week was an exception for the Broncos, whose flurry of turnovers made up for their disastrous 1-of-12 performance on third down. The Seahawks boast the third-best defense in the NFL on third down, allowing just a 29-percent conversion rate on the season. Bo Nix and the entire offense must do significantly better in these situations to have a shot at winning in primetime. — Christopher Hart

What are your keys to Thursday night’s game?

item.title: AFC North Week 5 recap: Ravens on top after gutsy overtime win
item.description: All four AFC North teams remain above .500 heading into Week 6.
item.content:encoded:
The Ravens took the lead in the AFC North with their win in Week 5, though all four teams in the divisionremain over .500 through five weeks.

Baltimore Ravens (4-1)

Baltimore gutted out a road win without Lamar Jackson, beating the Atlanta Falcons 30-23 in overtime.

Tyler Huntley proved again why the Ravens have full confidence in him at quarterback in place of Jackson with a strong performance against the Falcons. He finished 24 of 32 through the air with 201 yards and two touchdowns, along with a third score on a quarterback sneak in overtime. Derrick Henry was the other star of the show, rushing 24 times for 102 yards and scoring on an 18-yard screen pass. Baltimore’s offense ran for a total of 208 yards against the top-ranked run defense entering the week. Rashod Bateman led the receivers with 62 yards on five catches, while Devontez Walker scored a touchdown on the final game-tying drive of regulation.

The Ravens defense struggled on third downs, but was otherwise solid against Atlanta’s high-powered offense. Mike Green, Tavius Robinson, and Trenton Simpson all had sacks on Michael Penix, while Malaki Starks led the team with 10 total tackles. Penix was injured on Robinson’s sack on the Falcons’ final drive of regulation, bringing Tua Tagovailoa onto the field. Tagovailoa then went on to throw a game-ending pick to Kyle Hamilton in overtime.

Cleveland Browns (3-2)

The Browns’ three-game win streak ended with a 17-12 loss to the New York Jets on the road.

Deshaun Watson was under constant fire from the Jets, being sacked eight times and losing a fumble. He finished the day 15 of 33 passing for 155 yards and a touchdown. Isaiah Bond was the leading receiver with 74 yards on three catches, while rookie second-rounder Denzel Boston was the recipient of Watson’s lone touchdown to go with 43 yards on three receptions. Fellow rookie receiver KC Concepcion left the game with a concussion. Cleveland’s ground game continues to struggle as Quinshon Judkins finished with just 44 yards on 14 carries.

Carson Schwesinger suffered a Grade 1 ankle sprain against New York, but is considered day-to-day. The reigning Defensive Rookie of the Year had eight total tackles while forcing a fumble on a sack that was recovered by Adin Huntington. Huntington, Maliek Collins, and Sam Kamara combined for the other three sacks on Jets quarterback Geno Smith while Quincy Williams led the defense with 11 total tackles.

Pittsburgh Steelers (3-2)

The Steelers rebounded in Week 5 with a 34-22 home win against the Indianapolis Colts.

It was the Jaylen Warren show for Pittsburgh’s offense on Sunday. Warren accounted for 188 total yards, with 101 coming on the ground and 87 as a receiver. His two biggest plays of the day were both touchdowns, the first on an 80-yard catch-and-run and the second on a 50-yard rush. Pat Freiermuth had two touchdown catches to go with 44 yards on five receptions. Aaron Rodgers was on point in the passing game, completing 22 of 31 passes for 235 yards and three touchdowns while only being sacked once. Rodgers lost another of his top receivers during the game, however, as Roman Wilson is expected to miss time with a finger injury. This comes just after wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. was placed on injured reserve with a foot injury prior to Sunday’s game.

Cameron Heyward had the only sack for the Steelers’ defense. Payton Wilson led the team with 10 total tackles. Pittsburgh’s defense consistently held the Colts’ offense to field goals, with 15 of their final 22 points coming from the leg of Spencer Shrader.

Cincinnati Bengals (3-2)

The Bengals got back in the win column before their bye week with a 31-24 road win over the Miami Dolphins.

Joe Burrow was on fire on Sunday, tossing four touchdowns while completing 23 of 32 pass attempts for 190 yards. Ja’Marr Chase had another highlight-reel touchdown catch while racking up 77 yards on six receptions. Tanner Hudson, Samaje Perine, and Mike Gesicki were the targets on Burrow’s other three touchdowns. Perine led the team in rushing with 68 yards on 14 carries, finishing with one more carry than Chase Brown, who rushed for 39 yards and coughed up a fumble.

Cincinnati’s defense allowed 217 total rushing yards on the day. The unit faired better against the pass, as Jordan Battle snagged two interceptions off Malik Willis, who finished with just 137 yards through the air. The defense also sacked Willis three times, with Barrett Carter, Jonathan Allen, and Boye Mafe all getting home. Carter led the team with 11 total tackles.

item.title: Cowboys Week 6 opponent: A look at the 2026 Green Bay Packers
item.description: How nervous do the Packers make you?
item.content:encoded:
Green Bay enters Week 6 at 3-2 after dismantling the Chicago Bears 31-7, while Dallas sits at 2-3 following its debilitating 24-16 loss to Tampa Bay. The Packers are coming off a performance in which Jordan Love threw for 367 yards and two touchdowns, Christian Watson delivered a pair of scoring receptions, and the defense forced five turnovers.

The Cowboys have plenty of their own offensive firepower, but this matchup could come down to whether they can slow down Love and a Green Bay passing attack that looked particularly dangerous against Chicago. Here’s what Cowboys fans need to know about Green Bay heading into Week 6.

Jordan Love is coming off his best game of the season

Love has been productive throughout the first five weeks, but his performance against Chicago was a reminder of how dangerous he can be when the Packers’ passing game is clicking. Love completed 25 of 31 passes for 367 yards and two touchdowns, finishing with a 137.5 passer rating. He repeatedly attacked downfield, found receivers in space and took advantage of a Chicago defense that struggled to contain the Packers’ explosive plays.

Through five games, Love has thrown for 1,408 yards, 10 touchdowns and three interceptions. His completion rate sits at 60.5%, and his 95.5 passer rating reflects a quarterback who has generally protected the football while producing big plays.

Love’s deep-ball ability is especially concerning. Against Chicago, he completed six of eight passes thrown at least 20 yards downfield for 258 yards. When given time to throw, he has the arm strength and accuracy to turn a relatively ordinary drive into a scoring opportunity in a matter of seconds.

Christian Watson could be a nightmare matchup

If there is one Green Bay receiver Cowboys fans should be watching closely, it is Christian Watson. Watson is coming off a six-catch, 143-yard, two-touchdown performance against Chicago, including a 53-yard touchdown reception that helped put the game away. His first touchdown came on a 42-yard connection with Love, illustrating how quickly the Packers can produce explosive plays when their quarterback and receivers find their rhythm.

Through five games, Watson has 26 receptions for 474 yards and six touchdowns, averaging 18.2 yards per catch. That average illustrates the problem he presents for opposing defenses: Watson can turn a routine completion into a major gain, and he has the speed to stretch the field vertically.

Watson is not Green Bay’s only option, either. Matthew Golden had six catches for 123 yards against Chicago, while tight end Tucker Kraft remains another important target for Love. The Packers demonstrated that they can spread the ball around and punish a defense that commits too much attention to one receiver.

Green Bay’s defense is creating turnovers

The Packers’ defensive performance against Chicago showed why this matchup is about more than Love and Watson. Green Bay intercepted Chicago quarterbacks three times, including two interceptions by safety Xavier McKinney, and recovered two fumbles. The Packers finished with five takeaways and converted those turnovers into 15 points while keeping their own side of the ledger clean.

That performance pushed Green Bay’s season total to seven interceptions through five games, alongside 14 sacks. McKinney is an important part of this Green Bay defense. His two interceptions against Chicago highlighted his ability to capitalize when opposing quarterbacks make mistakes, and the Packers have several other defenders capable of disrupting the passing game.

Micah Parsons’ potential return against Dallas has been one of the more intriguing storylines surrounding this matchup before the season. Parsons tore his ACL in December 2025 and has been working through a lengthy rehabilitation. While initially having hope he could return against his own team, Parsons is not ready to begin practice this week, meaning he’ll miss the game.

Green Bay has already demonstrated that it can generate sacks and turnovers without Parsons in the lineup. The irony is difficult to ignore. Dallas traded Parsons to Green Bay in 2025 and later acquired Rashan Gary from the Packers as part of its effort to rebuild its own pass rush. Five games into the season, Green Bay has been considerably more productive at creating negative plays.

The Packers’ defense has shown that it can disrupt an opponent’s rhythm and turn mistakes into points. Dallas cannot afford to be careless with the football, particularly against a secondary that has made takeaways a central part of its early-season success.

A trip to Lambeau brings plenty of Cowboys history

The Cowboys and Packers have one of the NFL’s most recognizable rivalries, shaped by decades of memorable regular-season games and postseason meetings. The overall series has been competitive, but recent trips to Lambeau Field have generally been difficult for Dallas.

The Cowboys’ last regular-season win at Lambeau came in October 2016, when rookie Dak Prescott and Dallas defeated Green Bay 30-16. More recently, the Packers have repeatedly been the team to deliver the most painful blows in this rivalry. Green Bay defeated Dallas 48-32 in the 2023 season’s wild-card beatdown. The Cowboys’ most recent regular-season meeting with Green Bay was a 40-40 tie in September 2025, in Arlington.

Overall the Packers lead the all-time series against the Cowboys 22-17-1, and Dallas is 2-10 all-time at Lambeau. The historical context doesn’t decide Sunday’s game, but it does add another layer to a matchup in which Dallas needs to prove it can compete against one of the NFC’s more dangerous teams in a difficult road environment.

The Packers are not invulnerable. Their offense had been inconsistent before the Chicago game, and they, like the Cowboys could still be looking for answers.
